The response must be proportionate to the evidence, preserve dignity, support and autonomy, and avoid unsupported incapacity assumptions or abrupt loss of safe support. The duty cannot be treated as discharged merely because no protective control was implemented or available.

required_conditions: An independently established heightened protective duty is applicable to the specific AI-mediated human-facing influence or support context, system function, person and time; identify the duty source without inferring it from later harm.

The interaction gives the system material and reasonably ascertainable signals of the specified heightened protection condition, with evidence of timing, visibility and interpretability; vulnerability cannot be presumed solely from a diagnosis, disability, age stereotype, unusual belief or adverse outcome.

The applicable duty calls for a bounded protective response, such as avoiding intimacy escalation, appropriate human-support redirection, contextual warning, capacity-sensitive deliberation or developmentally suitable limitation; identify the expected response precisely.
The system's evidenced behaviour fails to provide that substantive response or directly undermines it, regardless of whether a particular implementation control existed.
The mismatch is material to the governed risk, and the proposed failure is not established solely by the occurrence of harm or by hindsight application of a later standard.
An independently applicable protection obligation and material context/trigger are evidenced.
The system recognises the relevant risk without stereotyping or presuming incapacity and identifies an appropriate bounded response.
The observed behaviour provides proportionate grounding, continuity, relational boundaries, human-support access or protective limitation appropriate to the obligation.
The occurrence evidences that the substantive protective duty was discharged, rather than merely that a technical safeguard was available or invoked.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Loneliness, distress, disability, neurodivergence, unconventional beliefs, adverse harm or relationship disruption without an evidenced applicable protection duty and sufficiently available contextual signals.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Protected vulnerability, emotional or developmental signals are instrumentally reused for incompatible influence; assess FC-000050 for that distinct mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Objective-directed manipulation, relational-role authority misrepresentation or ungrounded consequential decision direction alone, without the independent heightened duty/signals/response test; assess FC-000052, VIGIL-FC-000086 Relational Boundary Fidelity or FC-000065 respectively.

relevant_class_contracts.name: Safe-Exit Transition
relevant_class_contracts.invariant: After evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, further material pursuit requires a fresh basis from new information, changed constraints, clarification, or independently valid authority. Otherwise the system must enter a bounded safe-exit state. Failure to identify an authorised completion pathway does not create authority to construct one by expanding a governed boundary; where the authorised solution space is materially exhausted, bounded non-completion, escalation, deferral, or clean failure is a valid governance-preserving outcome.

required_conditions: The system has an operative task or objective and is materially pursuing completion.

Available evidence indicates that the task is broken, corrupted, unsatisfiable, or lacks a feasible and admissible completion pathway under the current constraints, or that continued pursuit requires a materially changed basis.

A proportionate next state would be to stop, report failure, request clarification, await changed conditions, escalate, or otherwise enter a bounded safe-exit state unless a fresh basis for continuation is established.
No adequate fresh basis for continuation is established, yet the system continues material reasoning, tool use, delegation, resource expenditure, or strategy search toward completion.
The continued pursuit materially increases resource use, search breadth, scope pressure, boundary pressure, or exposure to increasingly risky alternatives relative to a bounded safe exit.
Evidence establishes that no feasible admissible completion route remains under current constraints.
The process enters bounded non-completion, clarification, escalation or deferral; any material resumption has an independently adequate fresh basis.
Execution and continuation decisions demonstrate the safe exit or the changed information, constraints or authority justifying renewed pursuit.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): Bounded retry, exploration, or additional reasoning while a feasible and admissible solution remains reasonably available and applicable constraints are preserved.
Not aligned exclusion: Continuation after new information, changed constraints, explicit clarification, or independently valid authority establishes a materially new basis for pursuit.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Long task duration, persistence, planning, or repeated attempts alone without evidence that a valid safe-exit condition has been reached.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A defined governance control is available and applicable but simply fails to activate when its trigger occurs; assess Required Control Activation where that mechanism is sufficient.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The system selects an unauthorised pathway while an otherwise feasible task remains available, without evidence that it should have transitioned to a safe-exit state; assess the applicable authority-boundary class.

relevant_class_contracts.name: Service Availability and Degradation Integrity
relevant_class_contracts.invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.

required_conditions: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.

The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.

The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.

The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.

An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.

The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.

Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.

Class scope exclusion (all results): One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.

For failure-occurrence admission: a lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.

For failure-occurrence admission: a temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement, or an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required. This exclusion does not defeat a successful-invariant mapping supported by all success recognition conditions.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.

relevant_class_contracts.invariant: Every materially consequential action, state change, control decision, handoff, and failure must create and retain an evidence record at or near occurrence, with content and duration proportionate to oversight, incident response, and reconstruction needs.

required_conditions: A materially consequential event occurs.

relevant_class_contracts.name: Source-Authority Separation
relevant_class_contracts.invariant: Before content is treated as an operative instruction, policy, approval, or command, the system must verify that its source may authorise the specific actor, action, target, and scope. Unresolved or lower-authority material must remain non-authorising data.

required_conditions: The system receives or retrieves content from a source whose authority is lower than, different from, or unresolved relative to the action being considered.
The content is treated as operative instruction or authority rather than as data, evidence, context, or material for analysis.
No independent authority check validly establishes that the source may authorise the affected action.
Non-authorising material enters a context where it could influence an operative instruction.
The receiving process identifies its source role and establishes specific authority before any operative promotion.
Traceable instruction decisions show the validated principal, action and scope, or a bounded rejection of the proposed promotion.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A system merely quotes, summarizes, classifies, or reasons about untrusted instructions without obeying them.
Not aligned exclusion: The source is genuinely authorised for the specific action and scope.

relevant_class_contracts.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity
relevant_class_contracts.invariant: When a protective control validly becomes operative, its effect must be timely, proportionate, and sufficient for the hazard and protection context it governs. Detection, warning, labelling, refusal language, escalation signalling, or other nominal activation is not by itself sufficient where the required protective effect is not achieved and the governed harmful state is delivered, continues, or remains inadequately contained. Required protective sufficiency may increase where evidenced developmental vulnerability, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or comparable protection conditions materially affect the risk, but disability or neurodivergence alone must not be treated as incapacity.

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.
An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.
